name: Street Custom 'Spider Hole' Concealed Position Kit
product_name: Street Custom 'Spider Hole' Concealed Position Kit
description: A kit for creating a concealed observation or ambush position in urban environments — a camouflaged cover that blends with surrounding debris, trash, or construction materials, concealing a person at ground level. The kit includes a collapsible frame covered in adaptable fabric that can be dressed with local materials to match any urban surface — garbage, rubble, dirt, or construction waste. An operator inside a properly prepared Spider Hole is virtually invisible from any angle, and can observe or engage from a position that no one knows exists. The kit has a long history in Tier 1 warfare.

specifications.cover: Adaptable fabric for local material dressing
specifications.camouflage: Matches any urban surface with local materials
specifications.occupation time: Limited by operator endurance — typically 8-12 hours

story_hooks: A sniper operated from a Spider Hole in a trash heap for three days, waiting for a specific target — the position was never detected and was only found after the shooting when investigators followed the bullet trajectory backward.
A community defense network has established Spider Hole positions throughout a Tier 1 neighborhood, creating an invisible network of observers that monitors all movement through the area.

physical_description.visual_profile: A skeletal collapsible frame system resembling an industrial flat-pack, designed to disappear beneath layers of urban detritus. When deployed, it becomes a low-profile human-sized cavity invisible under camouflage dressing. The frame itself is utilitarian and angular—pure function with no aesthetic pretense.
physical_description.dimensions: Collapsed to 60cm x 40cm x 8cm; deployed footprint 2m x 1m x 0.5m (occupies ground-level cavity)
physical_description.weight_description: 2 kg total—lightweight enough for solo transport via backpack or cargo harness; frame alone ~1.2 kg, adaptable fabric covering ~0.8 kg
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum frame joints and struts; heavy-weave synthetic fiber base fabric (desert tan/industrial gray)
physical_description.finish: Matte anodize on frame to prevent reflection; fabric has subtle texture to break up surface definition; minimal sheen to avoid light catches
physical_description.color_scheme: Neutral industrial palette—matte gunmetal gray frame, base fabric in weathered khaki/concrete gray; no corporate branding colors
physical_description.interface_elements: Fabric attachment points (D-rings and velcro strips); optional periscope mount (quick-release); interior observation slits with subtle cross-stitching to prevent light bloom; collapsible hinges with positive click-lock mechanisms; minimal labeling
distinctive_features: Modular frame design with tool-free assembly via friction locks
Viewing slits engineered with internal baffles to eliminate silhouette glint
Attachment points for periscope optics (optional tier-1 package)
Dressing system: fabric loops and velcro grid for anchoring local trash/rubble/construction materials
Ventilation mesh hidden along bottom edges
Wear marks and stress fractures in anodize indicating field use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small embossed 'SC' logo on frame joint (almost illegible under grime); no visible price tags or regulatory stamps—designed for black market distribution
physical_description.condition_typical: Deployed units appear as innocuous urban debris piles—trash heaps, construction waste, collapsed cardboard—indistinguishable from environment. Stored units show minor dings and fabric fraying consistent with field equipment.

image_prompt: A Street Custom Spider Hole concealment kit displayed in two states on a grimy industrial workbench: left side shows the collapsed frame (aluminum struts and gray fabric bundle, 60cm length, partially coiled); right side shows a deployed unit photographed from above, disguised under a dressing of corrugated cardboard, crushed aluminum cans, and concrete dust, with barely-visible fabric edge peeking through debris. Low-angle dramatic lighting from a single halogen work lamp creates harsh shadows across the components, emphasizing the matte finishes and utilitarian design. Cyberpunk aesthetic: desaturated urban color palette, slight grain texture, cool blue overhead light mixed with warm tungsten bench lamp.
